thread.title: Apple: Here Are 3 Reasons for Optimism About iPhone Sales

author: David Marino-Nachison
title: Apple: Here Are 3 Reasons for Optimism About iPhone Sales
text:
Photo: Vasanth By David Marino-Nachison Sept. 7, 2018 1:47 p.m. ET Ahead of next week’s much-ballyhooed Apple (AAPL) event, at which the latest line of iPhones is expected to be revealed , new research offers reasons for optimism about how many of the phones the company can sell.
Apple reached a market value of $1 trillion on Thursday, propelled by the sustained success of the iPhone. WSJ's Spencer Jakab takes a look at how Apple got here. Photo illustration: Heather Seidel/The Wall Street Journal In a Friday note, Morgan Stanley analyst Katy Huberty suggested three reasons that consensus fiscal 2019 iPhone unit sales estimates—FactSet currently points toward 219 million, up from 217 million last year—may be too low as the replacement cycle lengthens more slowly than anticipated. (Morgan Stanley’s own estimates are currently in line with the consensus.)
Her reasons:
• Basically, people today can’t go for long without phones working at the top of their games.
“The smartphone has become many consumers’ primary device, resulting in increased usage/wear and tear and the need to maintain near-peak performance,” she wrote. “As a result, we don’t believe smartphone useful lives can extend much further, especially considering PC replacement cycles are currently about 4 years.”
Newsletter Sign-up • Several hundred million people are still using phones that are ripe for an upgrade.
“We estimate that 46% of the current iPhone installed base owns an iPhone 6s or older, equating to nearly 300 million iPhones that are three-plus years old and in need of a technological upgrade,” wrote Huberty. “In China, the largest smartphone market, this ratio is even higher at 55%.”
• Several likely technology upgrades may be compelling.
“We believe that integrating wireless charging, edge-to-edge displays, and front-facing 3D sensing/Face ID across a wider range of the iPhone portfolio, from the plus size high-end 6.5” OLED iPhone down to the “lower-end” 6.1” LCD iPhone, provides greater incentive for users to upgrade their phone over the next year vs. the current iPhone X/8 cycle,” Huberty wrote.
More About Barron’s Next Learn more about Barron’s Next The Barron’s Next 50 Morgan Stanley has a $245 price target, about 9% above current levels and 10% higher than FactSet’s mean, on Apple shares. The stock is up about 32% in 2018.
Meanwhile, we’ve covered a range of viewpoints on the stock recently, including one that gets into the importance of the iPhone , and other that talks about services growth .
